purpose: Role-depth tiers for the 2026 Week 10 official injury snapshot. Every tier is a statement about what the OFFICIAL pages say, never an inference about who will start.

tier_definitions.counts_as: starter loss confirmed by the league

tier_definitions.rule: Practice status is DNP and the Game Status column is blank.
tier_definitions.counts_as: starter at risk; NOT a confirmed absence

tier_definitions.rule: Official game status is Questionable or Doubtful.
Limited participation with no game status.

coverage.note: Tier 1-2 depth (starter vs backup) can only be stated for the four clubs whose own depth chart this session opened. For the other 20 the position is published but the depth order is NOT, so the role column is blank and flagged. That is the honest limit of the brief's '2nd/3rd/4th string' requirement today.

week10_findings.finding: Kerby Joseph is on the injury report (limited) but appears on no depth row; Brian Branch, listed first at the other safety slot, is also limited.
week10_findings.why_it_matters: A reported injury cannot be placed in the depth order from the club's page, so its lineup severity is unverified.

week10_findings.finding: Malik Harrison is Questionable and appears on no row of the Giants' published depth chart.
week10_findings.why_it_matters: The only Week 10 game status other than Out belongs to a player the club's chart does not place.

week10_findings.finding: 88 of the 93 players who did not practise carry no game status at all (94.6%). Only 5 have a final designation, all of them Out.
week10_findings.why_it_matters: This is the central availability finding: mid-week the official page tells you who is hurt and how much they practised, but it does not yet say whether they will play. Any injury signal built before the final report is therefore a practice-status signal, not an availability signal, and must be modelled as such.

structural_gaps.gap: No league-wide official depth chart. NFL.com /depth-charts and every /teams/<club>/depth-chart/ tested returned 404 on 2026-11-12; only club sites publish, and NE and DET label theirs unofficial in the page text.
No official snap-count or participation page at nextgenstats.nfl.com/stats/participation (404). Replacement exposure therefore cannot be measured from an official source.
The official injury page carries no date, timestamp or version. A snapshot is only as good as the hour it was taken; the page itself does not say when it changed.
The official inactives page was empty when read ('Please check back soon'), so the last-instant availability list could not be captured for Week 10.
The injury-report 'Injuries' column is mostly blank: only 6 of 254 rows named a body part, so injury type cannot be used as a feature even though the column exists.
No official page quantifies how many points a starting player's absence is worth. Any such number in this project would be invented, so none is published.
